children: Iraq has completed land allocation procedures for waste-to-energy (projects, paving the way to finalise the contract and begin processing 3,000 tonnes of waste in Baghdad.

Baghdad Municipality spokesperson Uday al-Jundail said the amount of waste collected daily in Baghdad Governorate ranges between 9,000 and 10,000 tonnes, noting that there is a plan to recycle it, in addition to an investment project awarded to a specialised company to process 3,000 tonnes of waste and produce 100 megawatts (MW) of electricity.

He told the Iraqi News Agency that the Municipality has finalised land plots outside the Baghdad Governorate boundaries, in accordance with environmental regulations, in the Abu Ghraib and Nahrawan areas.

These plots have been awarded as investment projects in cooperation with the Ministries of Electricity and Environment and the National Investment Commission (NIC) to a specialised Chinese company, he said.
“We are currently working to finalize the contract and begin processing the waste by incinerating 3,000 tonnes of it,” Al-Jundail said.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Iraq allocates land for waste-to-energy project
